title: Weingart
description: A song credit set like a forme of hand-set metal type: three lines of title on a flush-left margin, a process-red running time, one heavy brass rule under the title, the writer's credit on the margin and the red's baseline, the colophon hung on the figure's edge. Every line is a row of single sorts locked to the margin by its first letter. Push a line down and it hinges there a step at a time, far letter first, until it breaks into a staircase; a line that lands on the next one shoves it, and the title nests into stairs. The stair is the type's alone. The rule is one length of brass and only moves whole: the moment a letter comes down into it, it drops in one knock to the foot of the forme, across the feet of the red, where black over red prints a third, darker ink.
intent: After Wolfgang Weingart's Basel letterpress experiments and his stepped Typografische Monatsblätter covers (1972–73): Swiss order broken from inside the system, using the real constraints of a press, quantised steps, letterspacing and overprinting, to make new rhythm. https://neugraphic.com/weingart/weingart-text2.html
